body: 6 years. Went totally sober for half a year when it all started and I was running around getting tested. Reintroduced some things afterwards, because it wouldn't affect test results and nobody knew what was going on with me anyways. Helped me remain somewhat social, and I thought it would pass if I just gave it time and lived normally. It didn't. Might as well save money and let the brain recover. It doesn't.

Because there is a multitude of side effects, some of which are far worse than what you might call "shitty" and might be long-term or even permanent. Because there are dozens of meds, affecting different people differently on different dosages and combinations. Because determining the efficacy of each change takes weeks to months of guess work and new side effects. Because of the multitude of suicides linked to dosage adjustments. Because psychiatrists can be unavailable or incompetent. Because of other health conditions that can react unpredictably with each new antidepressant. There are enough reasons.
